items.item_text: 01. Information I provide to the following supplemental questions will be reviewed as part of the application process. Questions that are not fully and completely answered will be considered grounds for disqualification from the examination process. Stating "see resume" in lieu of a complete response to these questions is not acceptable. Select "Yes" to indicate that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes
02. Do you have a high school diploma or equivalent? Options: Yes | No
03. Have you completed an electrician apprenticeship program? Options: Yes | No
04. Please list the specific apprenticeship program that you completed, including the number of years completed. If no program was attended, type "N/A".
05. Do you have a valid California Driver's License (or an out of state license and are willing to obtain a California Driver's License upon offer of employment)? Options: Yes | No
06. How many years of verifiable, job related experience do you have performing journey-level electrical work? Options: None | Less than 1 year | 1-2 years | 3-4 years | 5 years or more

07. According to the job announcement, check the box that most closely matches your level of proficiency to perform the minimum qualifications listed: Installing, maintaining, repairing, and altering various electrical systems. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability and experience to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient and experienced in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

08. Inspecting and troubleshooting electrical systems, motors, controls and wiring. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability and experience to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient and experienced in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

09. Installing and maintaining power distribution, transformers, circuit breaker systems, electrical panel boards and emergency lighting systems. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability and experience to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient and experienced in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

10. Ensuring compliance with building, health and safety codes applicable to the electrical trade. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability and experience to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient and experienced in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

11. Interpreting trade manuals, blueprints, specifications, shop drawings, and instructions. Options: No ability to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Limited ability and experience to apply this knowledge in work-related situations. | Proficient and experienced in applying this knowledge in work-related situations.

12. The questions below are designed to indicate your willingness to perform the duty listed. Check YES if you are willing to perform this duty or NO if you are not. Please keep in mind that all of the duties listed are REQUIRED of the position. If you are not willing to do any one of the duties listed, you will not be considered in the recruitment process. Select "Yes" to indicate that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes
13. Working around and with machinery having moving parts. Options: Yes | No
14. Exposure to high voltage and electrical shock. Options: Yes | No
15. Working on ladders and scaffolding. Options: Yes | No
16. Working in a cramped or restrictive work chamber. Options: Yes | No
17. Exposure to fumes, dust and odors. Options: Yes | No
18. Describe the specific steps you would take to troubleshoot electrical systems within older buildings.
19. What safety issues are necessary to be considered when working with high voltage (over 600 V) electrical systems?
20. When performing a routine preventative maintenance of an electrical system, what are some specific items that should be inspected? Discuss why the inspection of these items are important.

Any combination equivalent to: Graduation from high school supplemented by completion of an approved apprenticeship program in field of specialty and four years journey-level electrical experience. LICENSES AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS: Valid California driver's license.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES: Perform journey-level electrical and specialized work involved in the installation, maintenance, repair and alterations of various District electrical systems; inspect and troubleshoot electrical systems, motors, controls and wiring; maintain records related to work performed. Install, repair and maintain electrical receptacles, switches, controls and lighting systems; replace fuses; assure power connection to fixtures and lighting controls. Install wire molds for computer labs; determine necessary circuits and evaluate breaker space; add new circuits; install conduit runs as required. Install and maintain power distribution, transformers, circuit breaker systems, electrical panel boards and emergency lighting systems. Maintain and repair a variety of mechanical and electrical equipment and systems including ovens, hot food carts, generators, exhaust fans and emergency lights and other related equipment. Install and maintain shop machinery and power tools; estimate costs and order parts, supplies and equipment for electrical projects; maintain related records. Communicate with other departments and administrators regarding projects and job requests. Operate a variety of electrical tools and equipment; drive a vehicle to assigned sites to conduct work; respond to emergency service calls as needed. Assure compliance with District policies and building, health and safety codes applicable to the electrical trade. Coordinate and direct the work of assigned helpers. Assist with maintenance and special projects as assigned. OTHER DUTIES: Perform related duties as assigned.

Methods, materials and equipment used in electrical installation, alterations and repair work. Principles and practices of electrical systems. Building, health and safety codes related to the electrical trade. Operation of hand and machine tools used in the electrical trade. Appropriate health and safety procedures. Technical aspects of field of specialty. Basic record-keeping techniques.

Perform skilled electrical repair and maintenance work. Operate a variety of electrical tools and equipment skillfully. Plan and lay out electrical work. Work from sketches, diagrams, blueprints, plans and specifications. Understand and follow oral and written instructions. Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others. Work independently with little direction. Maintain current knowledge of technological advances in the field. WORKING CONDITIONS: ENVIRONMENT: Indoor and outdoor environment. Driving a vehicle to conduct work. Exposure to fumes, dust and odors. PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling heavy objects. Dexterity of hands and fingers to operate various tools and equipment used in the electrical trade. Heavy physical labor. Bending at the waist, kneeling or crouching. Seeing to perform electrical duties. Climbing ladders and scaffolding. Standing for extended periods of time. Reaching overhead, above the shoulders and horizontally. HAZARDS: Working around and with machinery having moving parts. Exposure to high voltage and electrical shock. Working on ladders or scaffolding. Working in a cramped or restrictive work chamber. August 2016 Ewing Consulting, Inc.
